name: Virtual Try-On
tag: Shoppers see clothes and makeup on themselves before they buy, so fewer orders come back.

scenarios.title: Add try-on to a clothing store
scenarios.ask: Turn on try-on for our {skus} clothing products. We get {visitors} visitors a month and {returns} of orders come back.
steps: Pulled photos for {skus} products. {=round(skus * 0.92)} passed the image check; {=skus - round(skus * 0.92)} need a clean front shot.
Marked necklines, sleeves and hems so each item drapes on different body shapes.
Linked each size chart to try-on, so shoppers see fit notes next to the preview.
Set up the camera and photo-upload preview. Photos are processed for the preview and not kept.
Added tracking for try-on use, add-to-cart and returns on items shoppers tried first.

result.title: Try-on ready to launch
rows: Estimate from sample stores; results vary

followups: What about the products that failed the image check?
The {=skus - round(skus * 0.92)} items get a shot list for your photographer. Until then they show a normal product photo with no try-on button.
No. Try-on runs in the phone or desktop browser. Shoppers can use the camera or upload one photo.
Photos are used only to build the preview and are not stored by default. You choose the retention setting and the notice shoppers see.

scenarios.title: Match makeup shades
scenarios.ask: We sell {shades} makeup shades. Help shoppers find their match in {lighting} conditions.
steps: Measured the color of all {shades} shades from swatch photos and grouped them into {=max(3, round(shades / 6))} families.
Added a white-balance step for {lighting} photos so skin tone reads more evenly.
Suggests a top shade plus one lighter and one deeper option for each shopper.
Found {=max(1, round(shades / 25))} skin-tone ranges where the line has no close shade.
followups: Dim or warm light shifts how skin and product look on camera. The app asks the shopper to move to better light when the photo is too dark.
Can we use the gap report?
Yes. It lists the {=max(1, round(shades / 25))} tone ranges with no close shade, which is useful input for your next product launch.

scenarios.title: Estimate the sales impact
scenarios.ask: We get {orders} orders a month at ${aov} average. What could try-on mean for sales and returns?
steps: Assumed {usage} of shoppers try items on before buying.
Applied a sample 10% higher purchase rate for shoppers who try on.
Applied a sample 15% drop in returns for items tried on first.
followups: How would we check this for real?
Run try-on for half your visitors for four weeks and compare. The dashboard shows conversion and returns for both groups side by side.
Putting the try-on button next to Add to Cart and showing it on product pages with the most returns. Stores that do this often see usage above {usage}.
